doc.name: verificate-mcp-http
doc.instructions: Verificate Gate reviews AI-written code, plans and documents. Deterministic checks run first and can veto (placeholder or mock implementations, tests that cannot fail, standard-library calls that do not exist, secrets written to logs, unsupported completion claims); a Claude Haiku 5.5 review then checks the rest, including whether third-party API calls are real. Call validate_ai_output on a substantive change before presenting it as finished (documents and reports too, via validation_type), and validate_plan on a design before implementing it. Each result has one decision: approved, approved_with_conditions, rejected or incomplete. A rejected result lists findings with severities; address them and validate again. Submit one complete review unit with its callers, assumptions and test evidence in context; batch the fixes into one revision and resubmit with previous_receipt_id; dispute a finding with evidence in context.rebuttal. Unchanged input resubmitted after a rejection is flagged in the receipt as a repeat; change the code or add evidence before resubmitting. An incomplete decision means the review could not cover the scope; it is not a finding about the content, so follow next_action. The service reads submitted content and does not execute it. No token is needed to start: each machine gets 100 free validations.

tools.name: validate_artifact
tools.title: Gate a deployable artifact against the Verificate production doctrine
tools.description: Deterministic production-readiness gate for AI-built systems. Verifies the invariants that stop a system silently shipping broken: every critical component is PRESENT and LOADS, the import closure resolves (nothing assumed 'already on the box'), all runtime dependencies are declared, and health is a REAL fail-closed check. Returns approve/reject with a fix plan and ISO 27001 / ISO 5055 control evidence. Facts are gathered by the Verificate collector in your CI; the gate is the authority. Non-bypassable, fails closed. This is the control-plane sibling of validate_ai_output — code quality is one invariant; this gates the whole deployable.

artifact.description: Collected artifact facts: {critical_components:[{name,loads:bool}], import_closure_ok:bool, undeclared_deps:[str], health_truthful:bool}.

tools.name: validate_ai_output
tools.title: Gate AI-written output (code or documents)
tools.description: The merge gate for ANY AI-written output — code, documentation, reports, emails, configs: returns a binary approve/reject verdict with veto power — e.g. it rejects code calling the nonexistent stripe.Inventory API, an N+1 loop with the latency arithmetic to prove it, or a doc claiming success with no evidence. Deterministic checks (mock/placeholder veto, reward-gamed tests, standard-library calls that do not exist, secrets written to logs) run first and cannot be overridden; a Claude Haiku 5.5 review (ISO/IEC 25010, ISO/IEC 5055) then verifies third-party API calls and scores quality, accuracy, reliability and tech debt; its high/critical security and API findings block. In a benchmark, a frontier model reviewing alone caught reward-gaming and hallucinated APIs 0/6 times in a natural review workflow; this gate checks for both on every call. Read-only: nothing is executed. Call it on every AI-generated deliverable before accepting it; use validate_plan for plans, analyze_code for an advisory report without a verdict.

ai_output.description: The AI-generated output to gate — source code (a diff, function or whole file, any mainstream language) or prose (documentation, a report, an email, release notes). For reliable latency keep one submission under ~15,000 characters; split larger artifacts at natural boundaries (functions, SQL statements, sections) and validate the units separately. Reviews are wall-clock bounded: an over-budget model review returns an explicit timed-out result (deterministic gates still run) rather than hanging.

validation_type.description: What the output is: 'code_generation' (default) for source code; 'documentation', 'report', 'email', 'text', ... for prose (code-marker gates are skipped, integrity gates and the frontier review still run). Use 'report' (or 'status_report' / 'handover') for anything that CLAIMS work is done or passing: there, a completion claim with no evidence in the text is a veto. 'plan' for designs/specs.

context.description: Optional review context — an object like {"language": "cpp", "scale": "10k req/s", "unit_id": "U31", "goal_id": "G2", "delivery_drift": ["migration 048 applied, not committed"]} ('language' sharpens SDK-reality checks; unit_id/goal_id anchor the workflow guidance; delivery_drift lists work that is live or local but not landed on the remote) or a free-text sentence describing intent. Reviewed in full as untrusted reference data (it cannot instruct the reviewer or lift a veto); an oversized context is refused, never truncated. Put a dispute of a prior finding, with its evidence, in 'rebuttal'.

expected_input_sha256.description: Optional SHA-256 (hex) of the exact UTF-8 bytes you intend to submit. A mismatch is refused before any review, proving the gate saw the file you meant.

previous_receipt_id.description: Optional receipt_id of the review this submission revises or adjudicates; recorded to link the review history.

valid.description: True ONLY when decision is 'approved' or 'approved_with_conditions'. Rejected, incomplete and refused requests are all false.

decision.description: The one final gate decision (see decision_reasons, policy_version).

decision_reasons.description: Every rule that fired; `decisive` marks the ones that set the decision.

failure_class.description: input_error | transient_unavailable | incomplete_review | malformed_review | content_defect | deterministic_veto, or null when approved.

next_action.description: none | address_conditions | fix_and_resubmit | repair_input | retry_later_or_split | supply_missing_scope_or_split | retry_once_then_escalate | blocked_needs_adjudication

receipt.description: Execution receipt: receipt_id (unique per execution), input_sha256 (SHA-256 of the exact UTF-8 input), context_sha256, request_fingerprint (identifies an equivalent request; NOT an approval token), prompt_sha256 and versions, actual provider/model, completion state, elapsed time, scope reviewed/missing, deferred checks and the audit write outcome.

model_opinion.description: The model reviewer's own unmodified verdict/score; may differ from decision.

score.description: Blended 0-100 quality telemetry (gates fused with the model score). Not a probability of correctness and not the decision.

confidence.description: Legacy alias of score / 100. NOT a calibrated probability or accuracy.

issues.description: Severity-ranked findings, each 'severity|category|detail' with the reasoning

protection.description: Deterministic gate result. A veto here is final — the model review cannot override it.

vetoed.description: True if any veto gate failed the submission

vetoed_by.description: Names of the gates that vetoed, e.g. ['code_reality_gate']

provider.description: Model that ran the deep review, or 'protection-gates-only'

tools.name: validate_plan
tools.title: Gate an implementation plan
tools.description: The gate for PLANS, designs and specs — run BEFORE any code is written, the cheapest place to catch a bad design. Returns the same binary verdict shape as validate_ai_output, with findings on completeness, feasibility, performance and scalability implications, security risks and missing considerations (e.g. it rejects a plan that polls an API every 100ms per client, with the request-volume math). Read-only: nothing is executed or stored beyond the verdict. Use validate_ai_output for the code that follows.

plan.description: The implementation plan, design or spec to validate, as plain text or markdown — e.g. a numbered migration plan or an architecture sketch.

context.description: Optional constraints the review should weigh, e.g. {"system": "payments API", "scale": "1M users", "constraints": "PostgreSQL only"}.

tools.name: analyze_code
tools.title: Advisory code deep-dive
tools.description: Advisory deep-dive on existing code — scores and findings, deliberately NO pass/fail verdict, so it never blocks an agent. Surfaces performance hot paths, scalability cliffs, reliability gaps and tech debt with concrete latency/throughput arithmetic (e.g. 'O(n²) dedup: ~4s at 10k items'). Read-only: the code is analyzed, never executed. Use it to understand a validate_ai_output rejection or review inherited code; use validate_ai_output when you need an accept/reject decision.

code.description: The source code to analyze — a function, file or pasted excerpt.

analysis_type.description: Lens for the review: 'quality' (default, broad ISO/IEC 25010 pass) or a focused pass on one dimension.

language.description: Source language, e.g. 'python', 'typescript', 'cpp', 'sql', 'swift'. Inferred if omitted; stating it sharpens findings.

quality_score.description: 0-100 advisory score for the chosen lens

tools.name: generate_code
tools.title: Generate gated code
tools.description: Generate code and gate it in one step: an LLM writes the implementation, then the same protection engine as validate_ai_output vets it — retrying generation when the gate rejects. If every attempt is vetoed you still receive the last attempt, clearly marked validated:false with the gate findings — rejected code is never presented as clean. Generation runs on our infrastructure; nothing executes in your environment.

prompt.description: What to build, with any constraints worth enforcing — e.g. 'a rate-limited retry decorator with exponential backoff, stdlib only'.

language.description: Target language for the generated code, e.g. 'python' (default), 'typescript', 'go', 'sql'.

max_tokens.description: Generation budget. The default 4000 fits most functions/classes; raise it for multi-file scaffolds.

generated.description: False only when no provider returned code

validated.description: True if the protection gates approved the final attempt; false means the gate findings in 'protection' explain the veto

attempts.description: Generation attempts before approval or give-up

protection.description: Deterministic gate result. A veto here is final — the model review cannot override it.

vetoed.description: True if any veto gate failed the submission

vetoed_by.description: Names of the gates that vetoed, e.g. ['code_reality_gate']
